nana-asmau#text: Nana Asma'u was a daughter of Usman dan Fodio and was fluent in Arabic, Fulfulde, Hausa and Tuareg. She wrote poems on religion, history and the events of the jihad that survive to this day. For women in the countryside she built up a network of female teachers, known as the Yan Taru, who passed on knowledge in verse. She advised her brother Muhammad Bello on matters of state and law. In northern Nigeria she is still honored as a model for the education of women.
shaka#summary: The ruler who made the Zulu the strongest power in southeastern Africa from 1816.
shaka#text: Shaka was a son of the Zulu chief Senzangakhona and, according to tradition, grew up as an outsider. In the service of the Mthethwa ruler Dingiswayo he distinguished himself as a warrior and took over the leadership of the Zulu in 1816. He created an army of age regiments and a centrally directed kingdom into which numerous neighboring groups were incorporated. His rule was marked by great violence, especially after the death of his mother Nandi in 1827. In 1828 he was murdered by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana.
ranavalona-i#summary: The Merina queen who shielded Madagascar from European influence for over three decades.
ranavalona-i#text: Ranavalona I was the widow of Radama I and ascended the throne of the Merina kingdom in 1828. She saw European missionaries and traders as a danger to the independence and the traditional religion of her country. In 1835 she banned Christianity, had converts persecuted and expelled most foreigners. In 1845 her army repelled a joint attack by British and French warships on the port of Toamasina. European accounts painted a very negative picture of her; historians today also emphasize her commitment to the sovereignty of Madagascar.
ahmad-baba#summary: The most important scholar of Timbuktu, who was deported to Marrakesh after the Moroccan conquest.
ahmad-baba#text: Ahmad Baba came from a respected family of scholars in Timbuktu and owned a large library. After Morocco's conquest of Songhai he was taken to Marrakesh with other scholars in 1594, where he enjoyed high esteem despite his captivity. He wrote more than 40 works, including a biographical dictionary of Maliki jurists and a legal opinion against the enslavement of Muslims from West Africa. Only after the death of Sultan al-Mansur was he allowed to return to Timbuktu in 1608. The institute for the preservation of manuscripts there bears his name today.
tewodros-ii#summary: The emperor who ended the Era of the Princes in 1855 and reunited Ethiopia.
tewodros-ii#text: Tewodros II, originally Kassa Hailu, came from a noble family in western Ethiopia and rose as a warlord. After victories over the most powerful regional lords he had himself crowned emperor in 1855. He wanted to build a standing army, a central administration and his own arms production and to limit the power of the nobility and the church. In a dispute with Britain he had European envoys detained, whereupon a British army took his fortress of Magdala in 1868. Tewodros took his own life there.
pakal#summary: The best-known Maya king, under whom Palenque flourished and whose tomb in the Temple of the Inscriptions was discovered in 1952.
pakal#text: Pakal was born in 603 and became king of Palenque in 615 at the age of twelve; before him his mother Sak K'uk' had exercised power. He reigned for 68 years, longer than almost any other Maya ruler. During this time he strengthened his city after defeats by Calakmul and had splendid buildings with stucco reliefs erected. In the Temple of the Inscriptions he was buried in a stone sarcophagus with a jade mask. The carved image on the sarcophagus lid shows him passing into the underworld and is one of the best-known works of Maya art.
frau-sechs-himmel#summary: A Maya princess from Dos Pilas who refounded the dynasty of Naranjo as mother and regent.
frau-sechs-himmel#text: Lady Six Sky, in the Maya language Ix Wak Chan Ajaw, was a daughter of King Bajlaj Chan K'awiil of Dos Pilas, an ally of Calakmul. In 682 she came to Naranjo to renew its weakened royal house. Her son K'ahk' Tiliw Chan Chaak became king in 693 at the age of five, but she guided the fortunes of the city for a long time. On stelae she is shown standing over captives like a king, which was unusual for women. She died in 741.
jasaw-chan-kawiil#summary: The king who led Tikal to new greatness after a long period of weakness through his victory over Calakmul in 695.
jasaw-chan-kawiil#text: Jasaw Chan K'awiil ascended the throne of Tikal in 682, when the city was still suffering from the consequences of earlier defeats. In 695 he defeated the army of Calakmul, Tikal's great rival, and had the triumph depicted on carved lintels. Under his rule and that of his son, new temple pyramids and plazas were built at Tikal. He was buried in Temple I, the tall pyramid on the Great Plaza that is still the landmark of Tikal today.
siyaj-kahk#summary: A powerful stranger whose arrival at Tikal in 378 began a change of dynasty.
siyaj-kahk#text: Siyaj K'ahk', "Fire Is Born", is known from Maya inscriptions that report his arrival at Tikal in January 378. He probably came from Teotihuacan or acted on its behalf. On the day of his arrival the king of Tikal died, and shortly afterward a young ruler was installed whose father was connected with Teotihuacan. Siyaj K'ahk' is also named as an overlord in inscriptions of other Maya cities. Little is known about his origins and his later life.
senora-de-cao#summary: A woman of the Moche elite whose richly furnished tomb shows that women held the highest offices on the north coast of Peru.
senora-de-cao#text: In 2005 archaeologists discovered the mummy of a young woman, who had probably died in the 4th or 5th century, in the Huaca Cao Viejo pyramid at El Brujo. Her skin was covered with tattoos of snakes, spiders and other motifs. The tomb contained golden crowns, nose ornaments and war clubs that had otherwise been found only with male rulers. Her name is unknown. The find changed the view that only men ruled in Moche society.
itzcoatl#summary: The Mexica ruler who defeated the Tepanecs and founded the Aztec Triple Alliance.
itzcoatl#text: Itzcoatl, "Obsidian Serpent", became ruler of Tenochtitlan around 1427. Together with Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco and Tlacopan, he defeated the Tepanecs of Azcapotzalco in 1428, to whom the Mexica had previously paid tribute. In doing so he laid the foundation of the Aztec empire. According to later tradition, he had older pictorial manuscripts burned in order to spread a new history of the Mexica. His nephew Moctezuma I succeeded him on the throne in 1440.
nezahualcoyotl#role: Ruler of Texcoco, poet and builder
nezahualcoyotl#summary: The poet-king of Texcoco, co-founder of the Triple Alliance and builder of a great dike in Lake Texcoco.
nezahualcoyotl#text: As a young prince Nezahualcoyotl had to flee after the Tepanecs had killed his father, the ruler of Texcoco. In alliance with Tenochtitlan he regained his homeland in 1428 and ruled in Texcoco from 1431. He gave the city laws, supported scholars and artists and had gardens, palaces and aqueducts built. Under his direction a long dike was built that separated the fresh water around Tenochtitlan from the salty lake water and protected the city from floods. Poems in Nahuatl attributed to him are still read today.
moctezuma-i#summary: The Aztec ruler who extended the empire to the Gulf coast and enlarged Tenochtitlan.
moctezuma-i#text: Moctezuma I, a nephew of Itzcoatl, ruled from 1440 to 1469. His armies subjugated territories in the south and on the Gulf coast, from which Tenochtitlan received cotton, cacao and other goods as tribute. In the 1450s the valley suffered a severe famine after frost and drought. Moctezuma had storehouses built and the Templo Mayor enlarged. Together with Nezahualcoyotl he improved the capital's water supply.
ahuitzotl#summary: The warlike Aztec ruler under whom the empire expanded most.
ahuitzotl#text: Ahuitzotl ruled from 1486 to 1502 and led campaigns to the Pacific coast and into the area of today's Guatemala. In 1487 he had the enlarged twin pyramid of the Templo Mayor inaugurated with great festivities. He supported the long-distance traders, the pochteca, who also served as scouts. A new aqueduct that he had built led to a severe flood in Tenochtitlan around 1500. His successor was his nephew Moctezuma II.
tupac-yupanqui#summary: The son of Pachacuti who extended the Inca empire north and south through great conquests.
tupac-yupanqui#text: As a general under his father Pachacuti, Tupac Yupanqui already led the Inca armies, conquering the kingdom of Chimor and territories in today's Ecuador around 1470. Around 1471 he took power himself. He extended the empire southward into present-day Chile and eastward to the edge of the lowlands. Under him the administration with provinces and governors, the resettlements and the road network were further developed. He was succeeded around 1493 by his son Huayna Capac.
huayna-capac#summary: The last Inca to rule the undivided empire before an epidemic killed him.
huayna-capac#text: Huayna Capac took power around 1493 and ruled the Inca empire at the height of its extent. He waged long campaigns in the north, in today's Ecuador and on the border with Colombia, and often stayed in Tumipampa and Quito. Around 1527 he died of an epidemic, probably smallpox brought in by the Europeans. Because his designated heir also died, a civil war broke out between his sons Huáscar and Atahualpa that weakened the empire shortly before the arrival of the Spaniards.
kublai-khan#role: Mongol Great Khan and emperor of China
kublai-khan#summary: The grandson of Genghis Khan conquered all of China and founded the Yuan dynasty there.
kublai-khan#text: Kublai was a son of Tolui and of the astute Sorghaghtani Beki, who prepared her sons for rule. In 1260 he became Great Khan and prevailed in a four-year war against his brother Ariq Böke. He founded the Yuan dynasty in 1271, developed Dadu into his capital and completed the conquest of southern China in 1279. His attacks on Japan, Vietnam and Java, however, failed. Officials from many countries served at his court, including, by his own account, the Venetian Marco Polo.
hongwu-kaiser#role: Founder and first emperor of the Ming dynasty
hongwu-kaiser#summary: The son of poor peasants rose from mendicant monk to emperor and drove the Mongols out of China.
hongwu-kaiser#text: Zhu Yuanzhang lost his parents in a famine in 1344 and became a novice in a Buddhist monastery. As a leader in the Red Turban rebellion he defeated his rivals and proclaimed the Ming dynasty in 1368. He had the land surveyed, tax registers compiled and the villages organized into self-governing groups. Out of distrust he abolished the office of chancellor in 1380 and had tens of thousands of officials and their families executed in several purges. His rule was harsh, but it consolidated the power of the Ming.
yongle-kaiser#role: Third emperor of the Ming dynasty
yongle-kaiser#summary: The ambitious Ming emperor moved the capital to Beijing, had the Forbidden City built and sent Zheng He on great voyages.
yongle-kaiser#text: Zhu Di, a son of the Hongwu emperor, governed Beijing as a prince and defended the northern frontier. In a civil war from 1399 to 1402 he overthrew his nephew and took the throne. He had the enormous Yongle Encyclopedia compiled, the Forbidden City built and the Grand Canal restored. He led campaigns against the Mongols and had Vietnam occupied in 1407. Yongle died in 1424 on a campaign in Mongolia.
zheng-he#summary: The Muslim eunuch from Yunnan led seven great fleet expeditions for the Ming as far as East Africa.
zheng-he#text: Zheng He was born Ma He into a Muslim family in Yunnan; his father had made the pilgrimage to Mecca. As a boy he was captured when the Ming conquered Yunnan, was castrated and came to the court of Prince Zhu Di. He distinguished himself as an officer and was given the name Zheng. From 1405 to 1433 he commanded seven fleets that visited more than 30 countries around the Indian Ocean. He probably died on the return from the last voyage.
sejong-der-grosse#role: King of Korea of the Joseon dynasty
sejong-der-grosse#summary: The fourth king of Joseon promoted science and learning and created the Korean script Hangeul.
sejong-der-grosse#text: Sejong ascended the throne in 1418 and gathered young scholars in the Hall of Worthies to study history, law, medicine and agriculture. He had a handbook for farmers written and supported the inventor Jang Yeong-sil, who came from a low social rank and built water clocks and rain gauges. In 1443 he had the Hangeul script developed, which was promulgated in 1446. He secured the northern frontier against the Jurchen. Sejong is regarded in Korea as the greatest king and appears on the 10,000-won note.
schah-ismail-i#role: Founder of the Safavid Empire and shah of Persia
schah-ismail-i#summary: The leader of a Sufi order became shah as a youth and made Iran a Shia country.
schah-ismail-i#text: Ismail was the head of the Safavid order, whose followers revered him as a holy leader. With their help he captured Tabriz in 1501 and in the following years all of Iran and Iraq. He raised Twelver Shiism to the state religion and brought Shia scholars into the country. Under the name Khata'i he wrote poems in Turkish. After his defeat by the Ottomans at Chaldiran in 1514 he never again went to war in person.
babur#summary: The Central Asian prince from the family of Timur conquered northern India and founded the dynasty of the Great Mughals.
babur#text: Babur was born in the Fergana Valley and descended from Timur on his father's side and from Genghis Khan on his mother's. As a young man he repeatedly won and lost Samarkand until he took Kabul in 1504. From there he defeated the Sultan of Delhi at Panipat in 1526. In his autobiography written in Chagatai Turkish, the Baburnama, he writes frankly about wars, plants, gardens and his longing for his homeland. He died in Agra in 1530.
nur-jahan#summary: The wife of the Great Mughal Jahangir wielded the real power in the Mughal Empire for years.
nur-jahan#text: Nur Jahan, born Mihr un-Nissa into a Persian family, married the Great Mughal Jahangir in 1611. Because her husband was ill and marked by alcohol, she conducted much of the business of government; coins were struck in her name and decrees bore her seal. She promoted trade, fashion and architecture and had a tomb built for her parents in Agra that is considered a model for the Taj Mahal. Her niece Mumtaz Mahal was the wife of Shah Jahan. After Jahangir's death in 1627 she lived in retirement in Lahore.
schah-abbas-i#role: Shah of Persia of the Safavid dynasty
schah-abbas-i#summary: The most important Safavid ruler strengthened his empire through reforms and made Isfahan a world city.
schah-abbas-i#text: Abbas came to the throne in 1588 when the empire was hard pressed by the Ottomans and Uzbeks. He built a standing army of military slaves from the Caucasus and musketeers that limited the power of the Qizilbash. With it he recaptured Tabriz and Baghdad and in 1622, with English help, drove the Portuguese out of Hormuz. He promoted the silk trade and lavishly developed Isfahan. He was distrustful of potential rivals and had some of his own sons killed or blinded.
shah-jahan#summary: The Great Mughal had the Taj Mahal and the Red Fort in Delhi built and ruled the empire at the height of its splendour.
shah-jahan#text: Shah Jahan, a grandson of Akbar, ruled from 1628 to 1658. His reign is considered the golden age of Mughal architecture: besides the Taj Mahal he had the new capital Shahjahanabad built in Delhi with the Red Fort and the Friday Mosque. He had a Peacock Throne set with precious stones made. The enormous expenses and wars, however, weighed heavily on the peasants. In 1658 he was deposed by his son Aurangzeb, who kept him confined in Agra Fort until his death.
aurangzeb#summary: Under the last great Mughal ruler the empire reached its greatest extent, but also the limits of its power.
aurangzeb#text: Aurangzeb, a son of Shah Jahan, triumphed over his brothers in the struggle for the throne in 1658 and had his elder brother Dara Shikoh executed. He ruled for almost 50 years under the title Alamgir, conqueror of the world. Personally he lived modestly and strictly religiously; he banned music at court, reintroduced the tax on non-Muslims and had some temples destroyed. He spent the last 26 years of his life on campaigns in the Deccan. Whether his religious policy or the overstretching of the empire contributed more to its decline is still debated today.
oda-nobunaga#summary: The ruthless lord from Owari province began the unification of Japan with firearms and new methods.
oda-nobunaga#text: Nobunaga inherited a small domain and made his name with the victory at Okehazama in 1560. In 1568 he entered Kyoto and in 1573 deposed the last Ashikaga shogun. In 1571 he had the monastery complex on Mount Hiei burned down, he used musketeers at Nagashino and promoted free markets without guild restrictions. He was open towards the Portuguese Jesuits. In 1582 he was attacked at the Honnō-ji temple by his vassal Akechi Mitsuhide and took his own life.
toyotomi-hideyoshi#summary: The foot soldier of humble origins completed the unification of Japan and attacked Korea.
toyotomi-hideyoshi#text: In the service of Oda Nobunaga, Hideyoshi rose from common soldier to general. After Nobunaga's death he defeated his murderer and by 1590 had subjugated all the lords of Japan. Because he did not come from a noble lineage, he ruled not as shogun but as imperial regent. With the sword hunt of 1588 he disarmed the peasants, and a nationwide land survey fixed their dues. His invasions of Korea from 1592 failed; he died in 1598 at his Fushimi Castle.
yi-sun-sin#summary: The admiral defeated the Japanese fleet several times during the Imjin War and is regarded as a national hero in Korea.
yi-sun-sin#text: Shortly before the war Yi Sun-sin became commander of a fleet in south-western Korea and had the armoured turtle ships rebuilt. In 1592 he destroyed a large part of the Japanese fleet off Hansan Island, thereby cutting the invaders' supply lines. Because of intrigues at court he was dismissed and had to serve as a common soldier. Reinstated, he won at Myeongnyang in 1597 with only 13 ships against a far larger fleet. He was killed in December 1598 in the last naval battle of the war at Noryang.
matsuo-basho#summary: The most important poet of the Edo period made the short haiku poem an art form in its own right.
matsuo-basho#text: Bashō came from a low-ranking samurai family in Iga province and moved to Edo as a young man, where he taught poetry. He took his name from a banana plant that his students planted in front of his hut. His poems combine precise observation of nature with the spirit of Zen Buddhism; the most famous is the poem about a frog jumping into an old pond. His long journeys on foot produced travel diaries such as The Narrow Road to the Deep North. He died in Osaka in 1694 while on a journey.
kangxi#role: Emperor of China of the Qing dynasty
kangxi#summary: China's longest-reigning emperor consolidated Qing rule and promoted science and scholarship.
kangxi#text: Kangxi ascended the throne as a child in 1661 and reigned for 61 years. From 1673 to 1681 he crushed the Revolt of the Three Feudatories in the south, had Taiwan conquered in 1683 and concluded the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia in 1689. He had Jesuits at court teach him mathematics, astronomy and medicine and permitted Christian missionary work in 1692. He commissioned a great dictionary of Chinese characters. On several inspection tours of the south he won over Chinese scholars to Manchu rule.
qianlong#role: Emperor of China of the Qing dynasty
qianlong#summary: Under Kangxi's grandson the Qing empire reached its greatest extent and cultural splendour.
qianlong#text: Qianlong reigned from 1735 to 1796 and then abdicated so as not to sit on the throne longer than his grandfather Kangxi; he kept power until his death. In his campaigns he destroyed the Dzungar state and incorporated Xinjiang into the empire. He collected art, wrote tens of thousands of poems and had the great library of the Four Treasuries compiled, during which numerous books considered subversive were destroyed. In his last years corruption and rebellions spread. In 1793 he rejected Macartney's British embassy.
boris-jelzin#role: First freely elected president of Russia
boris-jelzin#summary: Stood up to the 1991 coup against Gorbachev and led Russia through the chaotic 1990s.
boris-jelzin#text: Yeltsin rose in the Communist Party, became party chief of Moscow under Gorbachev and later broke with the party leadership. In June 1991 he was elected president of the Russian Republic in a free election. When conservative communists staged a coup in August 1991, he called for resistance standing on a tank, and in December he agreed with the leaders of Ukraine and Belarus on the end of the Soviet Union. His rapid market reforms plunged many Russians into poverty, in 1993 he had the defiant parliament shelled, and in 1994 he began the war in Chechnya. On 31 December 1999 he resigned and handed power to Vladimir Putin.
wladimir-putin#summary: Has ruled Russia since 2000 as president or prime minister and in 2022 began the war of aggression against Ukraine.
wladimir-putin#text: Putin was born in Leningrad and served as an officer of the Soviet secret service KGB, among other places in Dresden. In the 1990s he made a career in the city administration of Saint Petersburg and in Moscow, became head of the domestic intelligence service in 1998 and prime minister in 1999. Since 2000 he has determined Russian politics as president, and between 2008 and 2012 as prime minister, creating an authoritarian system in which critics were persecuted and imprisoned; several prominent opponents died violently or in custody. He had Crimea annexed in 2014 and ordered the attack on Ukraine on 24 February 2022. In 2023 the International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant against him for the deportation of Ukrainian children.
osama-bin-laden#role: Founder and leader of the terrorist network al-Qaeda
osama-bin-laden#summary: As head of al-Qaeda he was responsible for the attacks of 11 September 2001.
osama-bin-laden#text: Bin Laden came from a wealthy family of building contractors in Saudi Arabia. In the 1980s he supported the war against the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan with money and fighters and in 1988 founded the organization al-Qaeda. From Afghanistan, where the Taliban gave him protection, he called for the fight against the United States and its allies and in 1998 had attacks carried out on American embassies in Kenya and Tanzania. He ordered the attacks of 11 September 2001 and then went into hiding. On 2 May 2011 American special forces killed him in his hideout in Abbottabad, Pakistan.
barack-obama#summary: From 2009 to 2017 he was the first African American president of the United States.
barack-obama#text: Obama was born in Honolulu, the son of a white American mother and a Kenyan father. He worked as a community organizer in Chicago, studied law at Harvard and then became a civil rights lawyer before entering the US Senate for Illinois in 2005. In November 2008 he won the presidential election and took office in the middle of the global financial crisis. He pushed through a health care reform, supported the Paris Climate Agreement and in 2011 had Osama bin Laden tracked down, but did not end the wars in the Middle East. In 2009 he received the Nobel Peace Prize.
xi-jinping#role: General Secretary of the Communist Party and President of China
xi-jinping#summary: Has led China since 2012 and has concentrated more power in his hands than any Chinese politician since Mao Zedong.
xi-jinping#text: Xi is the son of a revolutionary veteran who fell from favor; during the Cultural Revolution the young man was sent to the countryside. He rose through provincial offices and became General Secretary of the Communist Party in 2012 and state president in 2013. With a large anti-corruption campaign he also eliminated rivals within the party, and in 2018 he had the limit on the president's term of office abolished. In foreign policy China under his leadership acted more assertively with the New Silk Road and a strong military build-up. Criticism focuses on the oppression of the Uyghurs in Xinjiang, the restriction of freedoms in Hong Kong and the threats against Taiwan.
steve-jobs#role: Co-founder and head of the technology company Apple
steve-jobs#summary: With the Macintosh, iPod and iPhone he shaped the transformation of the computer and the mobile phone into everyday devices.
steve-jobs#text: In 1976 Jobs founded the company Apple in California with Steve Wozniak; with the Apple II and in 1984 with the Macintosh it made the personal computer popular. After a power struggle he had to leave Apple in 1985, founded the computer company NeXT and led the animation studio Pixar to success. In 1997 he returned to Apple and rescued the company with new products such as the iPod music player. With the iPhone of 2007 and the iPad of 2010 he changed the way people use technology. He died of cancer in 2011.
ellen-johnson-sirleaf#role: President of Liberia and Nobel Peace Prize laureate
ellen-johnson-sirleaf#summary: In 2006 she became Africa's first elected female head of state as president of war-torn Liberia.
ellen-johnson-sirleaf#text: Johnson Sirleaf studied economics in the United States, including at Harvard University, and was Liberia's finance minister before she had to go into exile because of her criticism of those in power and was imprisoned for a time. After the end of the civil wars she won the presidential election in 2005 and took office in January 2006. She worked for reconstruction, debt relief and reconciliation and led the country through the Ebola epidemic of 2014 to 2016. In 2011 she received the Nobel Peace Prize together with Leymah Gbowee and Tawakkol Karman for her commitment to the rights of women. In 2018 she peacefully handed over power to her elected successor.
wangari-maathai#role: Kenyan environmentalist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate
wangari-maathai#summary: She founded the Green Belt Movement and in 2004 became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.
wangari-maathai#text: Maathai studied biology in the United States and Germany and in 1971 became the first woman in East and Central Africa to earn a doctorate. In 1977 she founded the Green Belt Movement, in which above all rural women planted millions of trees to combat erosion, the shortage of firewood and poverty. Because she opposed land grabbing and Kenya's authoritarian government, she was arrested and beaten several times. After the change of government in 2002 she became a member of parliament and deputy environment minister. In 2004 she became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize, for her commitment to sustainable development, democracy and peace.
luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva#role: Trade unionist and President of Brazil
luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva#summary: Rose from metalworker to president of Brazil and reduced poverty with social programs.
